prompt.brief: Design a BitTorrent-like peer-to-peer file distribution system that splits large files into verifiable pieces, discovers healthy peers, and uses available upload bandwidth fairly.
successSignals: Make a signed torrent manifest and piece hashes authoritative while peer availability and transfer state remain ephemeral.
Use a tracker or DHT for discovery, rarest-piece selection for swarm health, and bounded peer sets to avoid connection explosions.
Verify every piece before assembly, resume partial downloads, and prevent malicious peers from poisoning the swarm.
Explain NAT traversal, seeding, fairness, abuse controls, privacy, tracker failure, and content takedown.

functional: Publish a file manifest, discover peers, request pieces, verify hashes, assemble the file, and seed completed pieces.
Show progress, peer health, piece availability, throughput, retry state, and integrity failures.
Support private swarms, signed manifests, revocation, trackerless discovery, and abuse or copyright reports.
nonFunctional: Target high aggregate utilization while keeping peer connection and control-message overhead bounded.
Support millions of swarms through DHT partitioning, tracker sharding, and short-lived peer liveness records.
Never accept an unverified piece; make manifest publication, piece requests, and resume checkpoints safe to retry.
Fall back from tracker to DHT and from rarest-piece peers to a limited seed set during partial outages.
scaleAssumptions: Support 10 million active swarms, 1 million concurrent peers, and files from 100 MB to 10 TB.
Partition discovery by info-hash and DHT bucket; cap peers per client and isolate very hot releases.
Persist manifests and moderation decisions while treating peer presence, choking state, and transfer progress as ephemeral.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the BitTorrent-like peer-to-peer file distribution s commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional BitTorrent-like peer-to-peer file distribution s writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return BitTorrent-like peer-to-peer file distribution s version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition BitTorrent-like peer-to-peer file distribution s by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound BitTorrent-like peer-to-peer file distribution s work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for BitTorrent-like peer-to-peer file distribution s projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable BitTorrent-like peer-to-peer file distribution s projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable BitTorrent-like peer-to-peer file distribution s records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure BitTorrent-like peer-to-peer file distribution s latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
